title: Introduce compatibility shim and point-in-time restore oracle
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed two upgrade classes cause unexpected failures in private deployments: non-backwards compatible schema edits and inconsistent restore ordering when replaying WAL/segment-based backups across heterogeneous clusters. This PR adds a lightweight compatibility shim that enables node-level schema adapters during rolling upgrades and a point-in-time (PTP) restore oracle that validates restore playbooks against a deterministic checkpoint before executing a customer restore. Summary: 1) compatibility-shim: an operator-side library that can register small per-table transformation hooks (rename/rename-column, default fill, index rebuild plan) applied as a staged migration step; the shim runs as part of the operator pre-drain hook so upgrades can proceed without an immediate full migration. 2) ptp-restore-oracle: a validation daemon that replays a restore plan against a read-only snapshot in an isolated namespace to detect ordering issues, incompatible constraints, or missing post-restore hooks. Design constraints: minimal operator footprint, no automatic destructive migrations, KMS-backed ephemeral keys for snapshot decrypt during dry-runs, and a safe-fallback path that quarantines tenants if validation fails. Included changes: Helm hooks to add a pre-upgrade job that runs the compatibility shim tests; Terraform module updates to create an optional IAM role and KMS key for restore dry-runs; operator changes to register, run, and report shim outcomes; CLI additions (installerctl) to trigger oracle dry-runs and export deterministic runbooks. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a helm value 'safety.compatShim=true' and 'safety.ptpOracle.enabled=false' by default. Canary flow: enable shim-only in Dedicated staging clusters for 2 weeks with nightly migration rehearsal on sampled tenant data; enable oracle in read-only mode for 1 week before allowing active restoration. Rollback: the shim is non-destructive and can be disabled; the operator includes idempotent undo markers for any metadata it writes. Checklist: - [x] Library and operator integration implemented - [x] Helm chart pre-upgrade job added - [x] Terraform IAM/KMS optional resources - [x] CLI commands and runbooks updated - [x] E2E rehearsal tests added in perf-canary harness - [x] QA: ran mixed-version cluster rehearsal on z1 and z2 clusters - [x] Security review for KMS usage completed Testing notes: unit tests for shim adapters, integration tests for isolated restore rehearsal, manual runbook executed with customer-like dataset and verified quarantine behavior. Backwards compatibility: shim only activates when explicitly enabled; no implicit schema changes. Related: ENG-4127 (migration reliability), ENG-4180 (restore automation).

release_notes: Added a compatibility shim to allow staged, non-destructive schema adapters during rolling upgrades; introduced a point-in-time restore oracle that validates restore playbooks against a read-only snapshot before live restores; new helm and terraform flags to opt-in for safety rehearsals; installerctl commands to run and inspect rehearsals.
notes_for_ops: Enable via helm: --set safety.compatShim=true --set safety.ptpOracle.enabled=true (start with ptpOracle.enabled=false to stage). For air-gapped installs set backup.kms.enabled=false and follow docs/private-deployments/compatibility-shim.md for manual key rotation. Monitor metric 'upgrade.preflight.failure_rate' and use 'installerctl ptp-oracle status' to inspect recent dry-run artifacts.
additional_context: This approach is intentionally conservative: we avoid automatic destructive changes, provide rehearsal capability for restore playbooks, and surface deterministic failure reasons so platform engineers can write targeted post-restore hooks. The shim pattern is extensible: future adapters will be shipped as small, audited modules in the operator repository.
